transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Torres, Rohan Patel, Elliot Chen (Redwood); Maya Singh, Leo Ramos, Jordan Price, Hannah Li (Pinecliff)

Summary (auto): Quick implementation kickoff to align networking, security, pilot scope, and ops handoff. Covering Hosted vs Dedicated options, VPC/on-prem considerations, SSO/KMS requirements, and immediate next steps to start a 2-week pilot.

Topics: onboarding runbook, network egress, VPC peering, SOC2 artifacts, Dedicated trial, pilot success metrics, rollout plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can wait a minute for folks to hop in, happy New Year, um, uh, from the Redwood side Rohan and Elliot are here, and I'm Ava, I'll run through agenda then hand off to Rohan for onboarding specifics.
[00:18] Maya Singh: Thanks, Ava. Happy 2026. We got the invite, excited to get this going. We've got some constraints around data residency and a couple compliance questions.
[00:28] Rohan Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda: 1) network & security handshake, 2) pilot scope & success metrics, 3) provisioning and runbook, 4) next steps. We'll also cover Dedicated vs Hosted briefly.
[00:38] Leo Ramos: Quick note, our infra team is WFH so might be on mobile. We'll try to get firewall folks later but want to map out the high level.
[00:45] Elliot Chen: Cool. I'll cover the ops steps, demo our onboarding scripts, and what we need for a trial Dedicated pool if you go that route.
[00:52] Jordan Price: For security — SOC2 report and key management are our top priorities. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:00] Elliot Chen: Yes, we have KMS integrations for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys through HSM/KMS options. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but can do BYOK in Private.
[01:12] Hannah Li: Can you spell BYOK? I keep hearing it spoken differently.
[01:15] Ava Torres: BYOK is bring-your-own-key, sorry for the acronym salad.
[01:18] Maya Singh: No worries. On data residency, we need logs retained for 12 months and we can't have tokenized PII hit any third-party endpoints.
[01:27] Rohan Patel: That's fine, we can set retention in the Console and redact or mask tokens; we'll need to map where those logs are stored for your audit. We'll share our SOC2 and data-flow doc after this meeting.
[01:38] Leo Ramos: Network question — are you requesting VPC peering or a VPN tunnel for Private? We run strict egress rules so if it's peering we need CIDR blocks.
[01:46] Elliot Chen: For Private deployment we typically do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud, VPN is also supported. For Hosted API we provide egress allow-list IPs. We'll add specifics to the runbook.
[01:58] Maya Singh: Great. Pilot scope — we want to test two production features: customer support assistant (low latency chat) and an embeddings-based search index. Latency SLO for chat is 150ms P95. Is that realistic?
[02:10] Elliot Chen: 150ms P95 is aggressive but achievable with Dedicated and appropriate batching configurations; with Hosted you might see 200–400ms depending on model and sequence length. We can give a perf baseline during the trial.
[02:23] Ava Torres: We'll include a benchmark checklist and default model recommendations. Also note quantization and kernel choices affect latency.
[02:31] Jordan Price: On the embeddings side, we need dedupe and retention policies. Also, where are embeddings stored? If they're stored in Redwood managed storage, do you encrypt at rest?
[02:40] Rohan Patel: Embeddings in Hosted are stored in encrypted volumes, at rest encryption enabled; for Private or Dedicated you control where they're stored. We'll document that.
[02:51] Hannah Li: Who will be our day-to-day contact for rollout issues?
[02:55] Rohan Patel: I'll be CSM point, Elliot is SE for technical issues, Ava for contract/exec escalations.
[03:02] [03:02] (brief phone join sound) Speaker 1: Sorry, I'm late, this is Leo on mobile.
[03:06] Leo Ramos: Quick follow-up — do you have an autoscaling policy for Dedicated? We can't have big cold-starts during peak retail hours.
[03:14] Elliot Chen: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with warm pools and burst capacity; you can set minimum instances and keep KV cache warm. We also support scheduled scale-up windows.
[03:25] Maya Singh: What's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private?
[03:29] Ava Torres: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood-managed infra with data isolation. Private is customer-managed control plane — usually VPC or on-prem — where you run the inference runtime in your network. Private gives you more control for compliance, but requires more ops on your side.
[03:45] Jordan Price: For our legal team we need audit logs and role-based access control, SSO via SAML. Can Redwood integrate with Okta?
[03:54] Rohan Patel: Yes Okta SAML SSO supported, and role-based permissions in the Console. Audit logs are available and we can set retention windows to match your needs.
[04:06] Hannah Li: For the pilot timeline — we were thinking two weeks of trial, then a ramp for a month. Does Redwood recommend a two-week proof window?
[04:14] Elliot Chen: Two weeks is a good initial sanity check, we usually do two weeks for smoke tests and then a 3–4 week pilot for performance & quality evals. We'll scope the required prompt sets.
[04:24] Maya Singh: On the quality side, can we pin model versions for deterministic behavior?
[04:28] Ava Torres: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants. We'll show that in the Console.
[04:37] Leo Ramos: Network specifics we need: list of egress IPs for Hosted, and for Private we'll share CIDR; also do you do mutual TLS?
[04:46] Elliot Chen: We support mTLS for Private endpoints, and mutual auth for on-prem setups. Egress IPs we'll include in the runbook link.
[04:55] [04:55] (small crosstalk)
[05:00] Rohan Patel: I'll drop the onboarding runbook link in the follow-up email — it has the sample terraform, boot scripts, and a checklist for firewall rules.
[05:08] Maya Singh: Perfect. For the embeddings indexing, we need an ingestion throughput estimate — how many qps can Dedicated handle?
[05:16] Elliot Chen: Depends on model size and batch config. For small embeddings models you can push hundreds of qps across multiple workers. We'll provide a throughput table and suggested batch sizes.
[05:25] Hannah Li: Any guidance on tokenization differences across models — we saw a drift in embeddings because of different tokenizers.
[05:32] Elliot Chen: Good point — tokenizer differences can affect embeddings. Part of our Optimize toolkit is to recommend model/quantization pairs and note tokenizer compatibility. We'll include recommendations in the benchmark sheet.
[05:45] Maya Singh: Security deep-dive — Jordan wants to confirm we can use customer-managed KMS and have full audit trail. Also need an SLA for retention and deletion.
[05:56] Jordan Price: Are there API-level hooks for data deletion? Our retention policy requires deletion on request within 72 hours.
[06:02] Rohan Patel: We have data deletion APIs and policy controls; for Private you control storage and deletion. For Hosted we'll run deletion jobs and provide proof in logs. We'll list the deletion API endpoints in the runbook.
[06:12] Leo Ramos: Can you also describe how KV cache warming is handled during deployments? We worry about cold starts.
[06:18] Elliot Chen: We support prewarming KV caches and continuous batching; during deploys you can keep warm replicas. Warm pools avoid cold-start latency. We can show a runbook for warm-up sequences.
[06:29] Ava Torres: Great. Let's talk schedule — proposed next milestones: runbook sent tomorrow, network info by 2026-01-12, pilot kickoff on 2026-01-20. Any blockers?
[06:39] Maya Singh: Legal needs SOC2 docs before kickoff, can you attach those?
[06:43] Rohan Patel: Yes we'll attach SOC2 Type II and DPA in the follow-up.
[06:50] Hannah Li: Also need to confirm data residency locations — which regions do you host in?
[06:55] Elliot Chen: Hosted regions include us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (limited). For Dedicated we can reserve in your preferred region based on capacity.
[07:06] Jordan Price: One more on encryption: are audit logs immutable? We require tamper-evident logs.
[07:12] Rohan Patel: We can provide append-only logs and integrate with your SIEM; for Private you can collect logs directly. We'll add detail to the security packet.
[07:21] Leo Ramos: For pilot instrumentation — what tracing hooks are available? We want per-request latency and model-level cost metrics.
[07:28] Elliot Chen: Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks; you can also stream events to your monitoring subsystem.
[07:38] Maya Singh: Will we need a dedicated account for billing during pilot?
[07:42] Ava Torres: We'll set you up with a trial account and apply trial credits; billing can be added later and you can opt for reserved capacity if you go Dedicated.
[07:49] Hannah Li: How does fallback work if a model variant is unavailable?
[07:53] Elliot Chen: We have policy-based routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to a lower-tier capacity to maintain uptime. Policies are configurable per-route.
[08:02] [08:02] (laughter)
[08:05] Rohan Patel: I want to call out the sample artifacts we'll send: runbook, network checklist, SOC2, DPA, benchmark template, pilot success rubric.
[08:14] Maya Singh: Sounds good. We'll review and schedule the security deep-dive.
[08:18] Leo Ramos: One operational ask — do you provide a terraform module for provisioning Dedicated endpoints?
[08:23] Elliot Chen: Yes we have terraform and helm charts for different deployment modes; we'll include module links.
[08:30] Ava Torres: Alright let's summarize action items and owners. Rohan you'll send the runbook and docs, Elliot will prepare benchmark checklist, Leo will share network topology, Maya will confirm success criteria, Jordan will schedule security follow-up.
[08:45] Maya Singh: Agreed. Any last questions?
[08:49] Hannah Li: No, thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[08:52] Ava Torres: Thanks all, we'll send follow-up within 24 hours and book the security deep-dive.
[08:57] (meeting ends)

References/Links Mentioned: onboarding runbook (link in follow-up), SOC2 & DPA (to be attached), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared)

Audio Notes: occasional mobile join, minor transcription errors (for example Somal for SAML in one place).
